note: Illustrative articles written by thinkingtext for the companies Wikinews rarely covers; used as shipped samples only when the Wikinews sample has fewer than three articles about the company. They are not news reports: every figure and quote is invented.

nvda.title: Nvidia raises outlook as data centre orders outrun supply
nvda.text:
Nvidia said on Wednesday that demand for its data centre chips continued to exceed what it can ship, and raised its revenue forecast for the current quarter above analysts' estimates.

The company reported quarterly revenue up sharply from a year earlier, led by sales of accelerators to cloud providers building out capacity for artificial intelligence workloads. Gross margin widened as the mix shifted toward its newest products.

The chief financial officer said supply constraints would ease gradually through the year as a second packaging partner comes on line, but that visibility into orders now extends several quarters.

Shares rose in extended trading. Analysts noted that the forecast implies continued growth in capital spending by the largest cloud customers, though several flagged that customer concentration remains a risk.

nvda.title: Washington widens export controls on advanced chips to China
nvda.text:
The US Commerce Department on Tuesday expanded restrictions on the sale of advanced semiconductors to China, closing routes that had allowed modified versions of high-end accelerators to be shipped there.

The rules take effect in thirty days. Nvidia, the largest maker of the chips covered, said in a filing that it expects a meaningful hit to data centre revenue in the region, which had accounted for a double-digit share of the segment, and that it would design products compliant with the new thresholds.

Analysts said the broader demand for the company's products from US and European cloud providers would absorb much of the shortfall, but that the move raises regulatory pressure on the whole sector and adds uncertainty to earnings forecasts for the coming year.

Shares of Nvidia and its competitors fell in early trading.

amd.title: AMD wins share in server processors as cloud providers diversify
amd.text:
Advanced Micro Devices reported quarterly results on Tuesday that beat expectations in its data centre segment, where sales of its server processors and AI accelerators rose strongly from a year earlier.

The company said several large cloud providers had increased orders as they sought a second supplier for AI hardware, and raised its full-year forecast for accelerator revenue. Its gaming segment declined, as expected, and the embedded business was flat.

AMD's chief executive said the company's market share in server processors reached a record, and that demand for AI chips remained strong across customers. Gross margin improved on the richer mix.

Shares rose after the close. Analysts cautioned that competitive pressure on AMD remains intense, with the market leader shipping its next generation of accelerators later this year.

amd.title: Chipmakers fall as PC demand forecast is cut
amd.text:
Shares of semiconductor companies fell on Thursday after a research firm cut its forecast for personal computer shipments this year, citing weaker consumer spending and a slower corporate refresh cycle.

AMD, which earns a substantial part of its revenue from processors for notebooks and desktops, dropped more than its peers. Intel also fell. The firm said inventory at PC makers had risen in the latest quarter and that orders for the second half would be lower than previously expected.

An analyst said the data centre business would continue to carry AMD's growth, but that the PC weakness would weigh on its profit margins this year, since the client segment had been recovering from a long downturn.

The company did not comment. It reports results later this month.

mu.title: Micron returns to profit as memory prices rebound
mu.text:
Micron Technology returned to profit in its latest quarter as prices for memory chips rebounded and demand from data centre customers for high-bandwidth memory used in AI systems outstripped supply.

The company said its high-bandwidth memory output for the year was sold out and that it had begun pricing contracts for the next year. Revenue rose strongly from the prior quarter and gross margin turned positive after several quarters of losses.

The chief executive said the memory industry's supply discipline, with producers holding back capacity additions, had helped prices recover faster than expected. Micron raised its capital spending plan to expand production of advanced memory.

Shares rose in after-hours trading. Analysts said the forecast for the coming quarter implied further margin expansion, though the memory market remains cyclical and consumer device demand is still soft.

mu.title: Memory prices slip as smartphone makers trim orders
mu.text:
Contract prices for memory chips fell for the first time in a year, according to industry trackers, as smartphone and PC makers reduced orders after building up inventory in the first half.

The drop weighed on shares of Micron Technology and its Asian competitors. Analysts said the decline was concentrated in commodity memory for consumer devices, while demand for the high-bandwidth memory used in data centres remained strong and supply tight.

Micron had said at its last earnings call that it expected pricing to hold through the year. One analyst cut his earnings forecasts for the company, citing the risk that weaker consumer demand would spread to other product lines, but kept a positive rating on the stock, pointing to the data centre business.

The company declined to comment ahead of its results next month.

pltr.title: Palantir lifts forecast on US commercial demand for AI platform
pltr.text:
Palantir Technologies raised its revenue forecast for the year on Monday after a quarter in which its US commercial business grew faster than expected, driven by customers adopting its artificial intelligence platform.

The company reported quarterly revenue above analysts' estimates and its largest ever operating profit. The number of US commercial customers rose sharply from a year earlier, and government revenue also grew, helped by new defence contracts.

The chief executive said demand for the AI platform was unprecedented and that the company was adding sales capacity to keep up. Palantir expects to remain profitable on an adjusted basis every quarter this year.

Shares jumped in extended trading. Some analysts said the valuation of Palantir already assumes years of rapid growth, and that the stock's rise leaves little room for a slowdown.

pltr.title: Software stocks fall as investors question AI spending returns
pltr.text:
Shares of enterprise software companies fell on Wednesday after a widely followed analyst report questioned how quickly businesses would see returns on their spending on artificial intelligence tools.

Palantir Technologies was among the biggest decliners, giving back part of a large gain this year. The report argued that many pilot projects had not yet turned into paid deployments and that budgets for next year were being set cautiously.

Palantir has said its own commercial pipeline is strong, and recently reported accelerating growth in the United States. An analyst who follows the company said the sell-off reflected its valuation more than any change in its business, but added that competitive pressure from larger software vendors adding AI features is increasing.

The broader market was little changed.

tsla.title: Tesla deliveries fall short as price cuts fail to lift demand
tsla.text:
Tesla delivered fewer vehicles in the quarter than analysts had expected, the company said on Tuesday, despite a series of price cuts aimed at lifting demand in the United States and China.

Deliveries fell from a year earlier. The company cited production changes at two factories and softer demand for electric vehicles in several markets, where competition from Chinese manufacturers has intensified.

Analysts said the shortfall would weigh on Tesla's profit margins, already compressed by the price cuts, and lowered their earnings forecasts for the year. Several said the company's growth prospects now depend on a lower-priced model and on its driver-assistance software, neither of which has a firm date.

Shares fell in early trading. Tesla reports full results later this month.

tsla.title: Regulator opens investigation into Tesla driver-assistance crashes
tsla.text:
The US road safety regulator said on Friday it had opened an investigation into Tesla's driver-assistance system after a series of crashes in conditions of reduced visibility, a step that could lead to a recall affecting millions of vehicles.

The agency said it would examine whether the system adequately detects and responds to fog, glare and dust. Tesla did not immediately comment. The company has said its software reduces accident rates when used as instructed.

The investigation adds to regulatory pressure on Tesla, which faces separate inquiries in Europe and legal action from families of crash victims. Analysts said a forced software change would be manageable, but that a recall requiring hardware changes would raise the company's costs significantly.

Shares fell after the announcement.

csco.title: Cisco beats estimates on security and AI networking orders
csco.text:
Cisco Systems reported quarterly revenue and profit above analysts' estimates on Wednesday, helped by growth in its security business and by orders from cloud providers for networking gear used in AI data centres.

The company said AI-related orders from large cloud customers reached a new high in the quarter, and that its security segment grew strongly following a large acquisition completed last year. Revenue from its core networking products was flat as enterprise customers worked through inventory.

Cisco raised its forecast for the full year. The chief executive said demand for the company's products from enterprise customers was stabilising after a year of digestion.

Shares rose in after-hours trading. Analysts noted that Cisco's growth remains slower than that of its newer competitors in AI networking, and that its profit margins will be tested by the shift toward software subscriptions.

csco.title: Cisco to cut jobs as it shifts spending toward AI and security
csco.text:
Cisco Systems said on Thursday it would cut several thousand jobs, around five percent of its workforce, as it redirects spending toward artificial intelligence, security and cloud products and away from slower-growing hardware lines.

The company expects restructuring charges this year and said the savings would be reinvested. It reported quarterly revenue slightly below a year earlier, in line with its forecast, as customers continued to delay orders for traditional networking equipment.

Analysts said the cuts would support Cisco's profit margins while the transition continues, but that the company's revenue growth prospects remain modest compared with the rest of the technology sector. The stock has lagged the Nasdaq-100 this year.

Shares were little changed after the announcement.
